# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Addressed both pending root-zone oxygenation amendments in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/substrate.rs`: added a defensive `.min(total_depth_cm)` clamp to `effective_penetration_cm` so floating-point edge cases cannot report penetration beyond bed depth, and expanded the `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown()` doc comment to explicitly document its fresh-registry read-only behavior versus the cached-registry hot path used by `step_substrate_zones()`.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Inspect the current substrate oxygenation path and the two pending review amendments to confirm whether the remaining work was a numeric safety fix, a behavior change, or documentation-only clarification.
2. [Completed] Patch `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown_with_registry` to clamp `effective_penetration_cm` to total substrate depth, and update the public `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown()` doc comment to clearly describe its fresh-registry semantics relative to `step_substrate_zones()`.
3. [Completed] Run formatting plus targeted and package-level `tank_core` validation to verify the clamp and documentation change did not regress substrate/root-zone behavior.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo test -p tank_core --lib systems::substrate::tests -- --nocapture` passed (24/24).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test root_zone_oxygenation -- --nocapture` passed (5/5).
- `cargo test -p tank_core` passed across the full `tank_core` package test suite.
- `cargo clippy -p tank_core -- -D warnings` passed.

## Outstanding Risks

- Validation in this pass covered the `tank_core` package; I did not rerun broader workspace packages such as `tank_harness`.
